anomalies.observed: R6 (1K) connects the fan connector signal pin J5.3 (net NET0001) to NET0005. NET0005 is the MCU reset net: it is on U1.1 / U4.1 (labelled RESET/PB5) and on J2.5 (RST of the AVR-ISP-6 header). The same fan pin J5.3 also connects through R7 (1K) to NET0008 (PB4), which carries the 5V1 clamp D2 and the pull-ups R2/R8 — i.e. NET0008 is the proper, clamped tachometer input.
anomalies.expected: The fan tachometer line (J5.3 / NET0001) should feed a single, clamped GPIO input (NET0008/PB4 via R7+D2). The MCU reset net (NET0005) must not be tied to a fan signal line: the open-collector tach node toggles and can swing to the fan supply voltage, so driving it into the reset pin through R6 pulls the reset line around, causing spurious resets and/or over-voltage on RESET/PB5.

evidence.quote: R6 1K between NET0005 and the wire from J5 pin 3 (NET0001); R7 1K between NET0001 and NET0008; D2 5V1 from NET0008 to GND (sheet /, page 1)
U1/U4 pin 1 = RESET/PB5 -> NET0005; J2 pin 5 = RST -> NET0005 (page 1 / page 2)

anomalies.impact: Whenever the fan pulls its tach line low (or drives it high toward the fan supply), the MCU reset pin is toggled/over-driven through R6, resetting the controller repeatedly and exposing the RESET/PB5 pin to a voltage it is not clamped for.
